old_description: Enter your email to stay in the loop on our latest collection drops, offers, and events!
about:
Florida Cracker Trading Company operates from Brooksville, Florida, branding itself as "The Original Floridian" with a lifestyle driven by the roots of Old Florida. The company's founding year, ownership structure, and founders' names are not disclosed in the available information.

The business sells a range of consumer products under the Florida Cracker Style label, including apparel such as T-shirts, hoodies, long-sleeves, and performance wear; headwear including flat-bill hats, structured and unstructured truckers, straw hats, beanies, and visors; accessories such as jewelry, bags, belts, patches, decals, drinkware, and kitchen goods; and a line of edibles featuring sauces, spices, rubs, bloody mary mix, salsas, jellies, honey, syrups, oils, vinegars, pickles, and okra. The website references a "Florida Cracker Kitchen" for the edible products, but no manufacturing processes, facility size, headcount, or production volumes are provided.

The company markets directly to consumers through its e-commerce site, with collections aimed at men, women, and children. Product themes reference Florida wildlife, state symbols, tailgate culture, and first-responder tributes. No B2B customers, industrial sectors, or wholesale programs are mentioned.

The brand positions itself around a "Florida Cracker Culture" that evokes a simpler time and southern hospitality, using slogans such as "In Grits We Trust" and "Eat Mo' Beef." No explicit statement about why the company was started or what differentiates its operations is provided beyond this cultural branding.

name: Florida Home Health Equipment
old_description: Your Premier Source for Home Medical Equipment & Healthcare Solutions
about:
Florida Home Health Equipment & Supplies (FHHES) operates from Orlando, Florida, where it has served the Central Florida region for over 25 years. The company is family-owned and operated, though the founding year and founders’ names are not publicly disclosed.

FHHES distributes a broad range of home medical equipment and supplies, including durable medical equipment (DME), respiratory therapy solutions, mobility aids, and specialized women’s health products such as breast pumps (Ardo, Medela, Motif), maternity and postpartum supplies, and post-mastectomy care items. The company also provides insurance navigation assistance for Medicare, Medicaid, and private plans, and offers delivery service to customers’ homes.

The customer base comprises individuals, families, and healthcare facilities throughout Central Florida. The company reports serving over 150,000 healthcare professionals and families worldwide, though that figure appears to be a marketing metric. Its product lines target home healthcare, respiratory therapy, mobility assistance, and women’s health markets.

FHHES emphasizes its family-owned, patient-focused approach as a differentiator, highlighting personalized service, expert guidance, and hassle-free insurance assistance. The business also stresses community commitment through education, outreach, and hands-on support.

about:
Florida Restaurant Equipment Professionals, Inc. (FLREPs) operates from its headquarters in Tampa, with additional offices in Central and South Florida. The company serves as a manufacturer's representative for premium foodservice equipment brands across the state. President Steve Smith leads a team of seasoned professionals including operations, culinary, and sales specialists.

FLREPs does not manufacture equipment; instead, it represents complete product lines from multiple manufacturers, providing specification support, product expertise, and live cooking demonstrations for dealers, specifiers, and end-users. The firm's coverage spans the entire state, with territory managers and marketing chefs supporting customers from the Panhandle to the Keys.

The company focuses on the foodservice industry, serving channels that include independent restaurants, chains, institutional kitchens, and K-12 school nutrition programs. Business development manager Linda Pierce specializes in the K-12 segment, while territory sales managers cover regional accounts.

FLREPs emphasizes its relationships with channel partners and the premium brands it represents, aiming to deliver total faceted coverage and experienced product support for every aspect of the foodservice industry.

name: Florida Torque Converter Corporation
old_description: We could not find a converter for your selection - let's try an
about:
Florida Torque Converter Corporation operates from Cape Coral, Florida, at 906 SE 9th Street. The company specializes in remanufacturing torque converters for automotive applications.

The company remanufactures torque converters using a process it calls blueprinting, where each component is inspected, machined, and balanced to exceed original specifications. Technicians keep original parts together throughout the process to maintain matched sets. The facility stocks thousands of converters for immediate shipment and offers custom stall-speed calibration for performance applications. Products cover OEM replacement, diesel performance, high-performance, and Jeep-specific units.

Customers include retail buyers purchasing online, wholesale distributors through a dedicated program, and enthusiasts seeking performance upgrades for diesel, high-performance, and Jeep vehicles. The company serves the automotive aftermarket across the United States.

Florida Torque Converter differentiates itself by its matched-part remanufacturing method, lifetime warranty on all units, and the ability to customize stall speeds to a vehicle's power curve. The blueprinting process aims to reduce vibration and extend component life beyond factory standards.

name: Food Concept Idaho
old_description: We design to your requirements at Food Concept Concession Trailers. We have been in the business for over 15 years. Tell us what you want to accomplish and we will make it happen.
about:
Food Concept Idaho operates from Nampa, Idaho, where Ozzie and Brenda Rodriguez founded the family-owned business to design and build custom concession trailers. Ozzie brings nearly 23 years of trailer design and fabrication experience, while Brenda contributes a background in customer service. The company emerged as food trucks gained popularity in the Treasure Valley.

The shop builds trailers from the ground up — chassis fabrication, welding, plumbing, electrical, cabinetry, and commercial appliance installation — all balanced for safe hauling. Every project starts with a detailed consultation to map workflow, equipment needs, and health-code compliance. The company reports more than 200 completed projects and over 150 custom designs, with a 100% inspection pass rate on new units. Warranties cover the structure for two years and appliances for one year through the manufacturer.

Customers range from independent coffee operators and taco vendors to specialty concepts like a mobile sushi bar converted from a bus. The company also serves clients needing cargo or toy-hauler trailers. Testimonials cite Bright Eyes Coffee, Tacos El Guey, and Basil and Bloom as repeat buyers.

The Rodriguezes attribute their speed and quality to their team, and they highlight a consultative approach that balances efficiency, comfort, and cost. Their differentiation rests on a 100% health-inspection pass rate, U.S.-built construction, and a willingness to tackle complex renovations such as the bus-based sushi bar.

name: Food Concepts, Inc. (FCI)
old_description: Food Concepts, Inc. creates USA-Made Fixtures, Graphics, and Modular Systems
about:
Food Concepts, Inc. (FCI) was founded on July 26, 1991 by Brad Duesler above his garage in Middleton, Wisconsin, with the goal of creating better solutions for foodservice operators. More than three decades later, the company remains headquartered in Middleton, just outside Madison, where its team designs, engineers, manufactures, prints, fulfills, and installs fixtures, graphics, and modular systems for customers across the United States.

FCI operates as a single-source partner, combining product design, manufacturing, large-format printing, CAD engineering, graphic design, fulfillment, logistics, and installation under one roof. Its patented proprietary systems include PanelRak™ modular merchandising, the EZ-Tilt Sneeze Guard™ for roller grills, MTF Cabinetry™ modular tube frame construction, MTF Foodservice Kiosk™ pop-up units, ImageTrak™ graphic rail systems, and a Modular Food Court System™. The company also runs two e-commerce arms: FOODPROS.com for foodservice equipment and supplies, and RollerGrill.com for commercial roller grill programs.

The company serves convenience stores, travel centers, grocery retailers, quick-service restaurants, hospitality venues, K‑12 schools, colleges and universities, healthcare facilities, military installations, stadiums, micromarkets, and tradeshow environments. Reference customers cited include Hunt Brothers Pizza, Southwest Georgia Oil Co., United Fast Food and Beverage, Team Saverino, Rocky Rococo Pizza and Pasta, Par Pacific (nomnom), and Driven Coffee.

FCI was started to solve everyday operational challenges in foodservice. The company emphasizes that innovation is purpose‑driven — creating products that make foodservice easier to operate and more profitable — and that having design, manufacturing, printing, and installation integrated allows projects to move faster with simpler communication.

name: Food Equip Parts & Services Co
old_description: This website is merely a representation of selected items that we stock or can supply.
about:
Organized in 1975, FEPSCO Inc. (Food Equip Parts & Service Co) was established in Honolulu, Hawaii, to address a gap in the local market for factory replacement parts and repair services for commercial foodservice equipment. The company has operated continuously under the FEPSCO name since its founding.

FEPSCO acts as an authorized parts distributor and service provider for a broad roster of U.S. foodservice equipment manufacturers, including Chicago Faucets, T&S Brass, Dormont, Edlund, and Wells. From its Honolulu facility, the company maintains a large inventory of parts and accessories — ranging from faucets and drain assemblies to gas connectors and can opener components — and provides both in-warranty and out-of-warranty repair services. It also supplies customers across the Pacific Rim, with most outbound shipments sent overnight to destinations such as Guam, the Marianas, American Samoa, and U.S. military installations in Okinawa, Japan, and Korea.

The company serves commercial kitchen operators of all types: restaurants, cafeterias, hospital foodservice departments, and military galleys and messes. Its customer base extends to institutional facilities and U.S. Army and Air Force bases throughout the Pacific. FEPSCO also offers technical assistance by phone, fax, or email, drawing on factory-printed and electronic documentation.

FEPSCO was created to fill a void in Hawaii's foodservice supply chain, and its differentiation lies in its manufacturer-authorized status, deep inventory, and ability to ship overnight across the Pacific. The firm emphasizes ready access to factory technical data and a willingness to source hard-to-find items on request.

old_description: We know our stuff and we’ve been here for over 30 years. We will continue to assist you even after the installation of the equipment.
about:
Food Equipment Representatives (FER) operates from its corporate headquarters in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, with a second office and test kitchen in Orlando. The company has served the Florida foodservice market for more than 30 years, acting as the direct factory representative for two dozen commercial kitchen equipment brands.

FER does not manufacture equipment itself; instead, it represents 23 product lines covering ovens, refrigeration, food preparation tools, and other high-performance kitchen systems. The firm provides product demonstrations and hands-on training at its two culinary centers, and it coordinates factory-authorized service and warranty assessments through a network of authorized technicians.

The company’s customers include restaurants, hotels, schools, and other foodservice establishments throughout Florida. FER’s role is to match each operation with equipment suited to its menu, volume, and space constraints, drawing on long-standing relationships with the manufacturers it represents.

FER emphasizes that its value extends beyond product sales, citing personalized consultation, ongoing support after installation, and the transfer of manufacturer-backed benefits to the end user as key differentiators. The firm’s longevity and manufacturer partnerships are presented as the foundation of its service model.
